bug_semantics: Apache MINA AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() deserializes untrusted Java streams. The CVE-2024-52046 allowlist was installed only in ObjectInputStream.resolveClass() after readClassDescriptor() already did Class.forName(className, true, classLoader), so a rejected class's <clinit> can run before the classname check. Attack path: any app that calls IoBuffer.getObject() (including via ObjectSerializationCodecFactory) and accepts attacker-controlled buffer bytes. CWE-502. CVE.org CNA Apache, state PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected).
flaw_origin: On 2.2.X, 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea (2024-11-04, message 'pom.xml') first added ClassNameMatcher acceptMatchers and a resolveClass() loop that accepts only allowlisted names, while leaving the existing Class.forName(..., true, ...) in readClassDescriptor() unguarded. Immediate parent 23e6ee17bae46bb8e7a76dd7aeb508ec89e76a25 still has the forName(true) deserializer but no allowlist. Same late-check pattern was later copied to 2.0.X (834396355766e0c8f6bbf0493d4588b3fa9d347d) and 2.1.X (cdb59eb6131696a440870ab89ad0e20804eb5ca7).
